The radius of \(B_n\) is the distance from the origin to any center, \(\sqrt n\), minus the radius \(1\) of the original balls:
\[
R_n=\sqrt n-1.
\]
For \(B_n\) to contain a point with a coordinate greater than \(2\), its radius must be strictly greater than \(2\):
\[
\sqrt n-1>2 \implies \sqrt n>3 \implies n>9.
\]
Thus the smallest integer is
\[
\boxed{10}.
\]
